1. General Staff: 78 combat clashes on front lines, enemy suffers significant losses in Avdiivka sector

In the past day, 78 combat engagements took place on the front lines. In the Avdiivka sector, the enemy keeps trying to encircle Avdiivka. Ukrainian soldiers hold the defense, inflicting significant losses on the enemy.

The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine said this in its morning update, Ukrinform reports.
More https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3783598-general-staff-78-combat-clashes-on-front-lines-enemy-suffers-significant-losses-in-avdiivka-sector.html

2. AFU General Staff: Rocket launchers hit another control point of Russians

Ukrainian aviation carried out five strikes on the Russian occupiers and one on the air defense system during the day, the rocket launchers hit, in particular, the enemy control point, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reports the situation as of 18:00 on Monday. "During the day, the aviation of the Defense Forces carried out five strikes on the areas of concentration of personnel, weapons and military equipment and one on the enemy's anti-aircraft missile system," the General Staff said in a Facebook message.

It is reported that units of the missile forces hit three artillery facilities, a control point and an area of concentration of personnel, weapons and military equipment of the enemy.

3. Klymenko: Enemy releases largest number of aerial bombs in Kherson region 87

Over the past day, the enemy has released 87 aerial bombs on the settlements of Kherson region, this is the largest number for the entire time of the war, Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko said on Telegram.

In addition, as a result of the shelling of Kherson on Sunday evening, four multi-storey buildings were damaged. At about 3 a.m., the invaders shelled the city again, two private houses were damaged.

Also at night, the enemy inflicted 12 airstrikes on the village of Krynki and the town of Beryslav.

The occupiers shelled Odesa on Sunday evening, as a result, 20 apartment buildings, an art museum, more than 20 cars, infrastructure were damaged, and fires broke out in two buildings. In the village of Usatove, a private house was damaged as a result of the attack. In total, as a result of the strike in Odesa region, eight people were injured.

4. Enemy shells Nikopol district three times with heavy artillery: one injured, church damaged

Since yesterday evening, Russian troops have shelled Nikopol district in Dnipropetrovsk region three times with heavy artillery, injuring one civilian.  

Serhiy Lysak, the head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration, said this in a Facebook post. "Since the evening, the enemy has hit Nikopol district three times with heavy artillery. A 56-year-old man was injured in Nikopol. He will be treated at home. The church was damaged. Seven private houses, an outbuilding, two cars were damaged, as well as a power line and gas pipelines," he wrote.

5. Army of drones hits record number of Russian strongholds Fedorov

Ukrainian UAV operators within the framework of the Army of Drones project during the past week, from October 30 to November 6, destroyed a record number of strongholds: 335 positions, as well as 83 armored combat vehicles, 72 trucks, 36 tanks and hundreds of occupiers, Deputy Prime Minister for Innovation, Development of Education, Science and Technology, Minister of Digital Transformation Mykhailo Fedorov said.

"Last week, the enemies were unlucky with strongholds: UAV operators damaged 335 positions which is an absolute record. Also among those affected are 83 armored fighting vehicles, 72 trucks, 36 tanks and hundreds of occupiers," he wrote on the Telegram channel on Monday.

6. Russia has increased production of missiles faster than expected - ISW

The Russian military has increased its own stockpile of high-precision missiles faster than expected in previous forecasts.

This was reported by Censor.NET with reference to the Institute for the Study of War (ISW).

According to the report, on November 6, Vadym Skibitskyi, spokesman for the Main Directorate of Military Intelligence (HUR) of Ukraine, said that Russian troops have 870 high-precision operational-strategic and strategic missiles in reserve.

Earlier, on August 28, Skibitskyi stated that Russian forces had 585 long-range missiles in reserve. That is, during this period, Russian forces increased their missile reserve by 285 missiles.

On 6 November, Skibitskyi added that in total, Russian forces produced 115 high-precision long-range missiles in October: 30 Iskander-M cruise missiles, 12 Iskander-K cruise missiles, 20 Kalibr cruise missiles, 40 Kh-101 cruise missiles, 9 Kh-32 cruise missiles and 4 Kinzhal ballistic missiles.
Source: https://censor.net/en/n3453979

7. Elections in Ukraine out of time Zelenskyy

President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that the elections in Ukraine are "not at the time." "I think that now is not the time for elections. And if you need to put an end to a particular political dispute and continue to work only in unity, then there are structures in the state that are able to put a period and give society all the necessary answers so that there is no space for conflicts and someone else's game against Ukraine," Zelenskyy said in a video message on Monday.

"My personal attitude and call, just like on February 24, is to take care of our state, its protection, the destruction of the occupier, the freedom of Ukraine, which is being acquired now in the battles for Ukraine," the President said.

8. EU calls info saying that reps of USA, EU discussing with Kyiv possibility of peace talks with Russia untrue

The European Union called untrue the information that representatives of the United States and the EU are discussing with the Ukrainian side possible peace talks with the Russian Federation.

A senior European diplomat told reporters about this in Brussels on Monday on condition of anonymity. If it was true I supposed I should know. I guess it s not true, he said.

Answering a question from the Interfax-Ukraine agency about a possible revision of the types of weapons supplied by the EU to Ukraine in connection with the latest assessment of the situation on the battlefield, which was given by Commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Valeriy Zaluzhny in his article, the interlocutor of journalists noted that "the one who is on the way is air support." "A famous F16. This is the first thing that could come in order to increase the level of the capacity of the Ukrainian army," he believes. As it is known, in an article for the Economist publication, Zaluzhny stated that the war had moved into a positional phase due to modern technologies owned by both sides.

The high-ranking European diplomat also touched upon the issue of preparing Ukraine, which is at war, for EU membership. Noting that as of today he does not know the content of the recommendations of the European Commission regarding the possible start of membership negotiations, he said that they shouldn t wait for the end of the war so that Ukraine could prepare itself for membership. He added that this is what Ukraine wants to do, and will be supported on this way.

As known, on November 8, the European Commission will publish the so-called "expansion package", which will assess the progress of Ukraine, which has the status of a candidate, in implementing the recommendations, the implementation of which is necessary for the start of membership negotiations.

9. European Commission head calls military support, Ukraine's admission into EU geostrategic interests of Europe

President of the European Commission (EC), Ursula von der Leyen, speaking at the conference of EU ambassadors, said: the European Union, helping Ukraine, "must try to focus on the way forward, " and formulated three goals of such support. The first objective must be to continue to work for a just and lasting peace, not another frozen conflict (&)The main pathway to achieve this is President Zelenskyy's Peace Formula.

That is why, we, the Commission, participated in all three meetings of National Security Advisers, the head of the European Commission said in Brussels on Monday.

Second, von der Leyen continued, the EU has to ensure a sustained military force capable of defending Ukraine now and (&) in the future. This has, of course, strong implications for our defence industry. We must step up our production capacities. This is why we have introduced ASAP, the Act in Support of Ammunition Production. But we must, of course, also look beyond ammunition. We have to look at air defence which is crucial at the moment being , maritime capabilities, but, of course, for the mid and long term, also cyber and space. (&) We have to ensure now that no industrial bottleneck prevents us from protecting Europe and giving our full support to Ukraine, the EC president explained.

My third point: The best way to give Ukraine stability and prosperity in the mid and long term is, of course, Membership in the European Union. Just think about it, to make Ukraine recover Europe is the answer. To strengthen Ukraine's democracy even further Europe is the answer. To protect Ukraine (&), Europe is the answer, von der Leyen said.

She added that it is clearly in Europe's geostrategic interest to complete our Union.

10. Slovakia not to supply Ukraine with weapons from army depots, but not going to hinder supply of private companies PM

Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico said on Monday that the authorities will not transfer weapons for Ukraine from the arsenals of the Slovak army, but they are not going to hinder the supply of private manufacturers. "We have explained this often, and I want to clarify: in this case we are talking about weapons, ammunition from Slovak army depots, about state resources," Western media quoted him as saying.

"But when a company wants to produce weapons and sell them somewhere, no one will put obstacles in its way," he continued.

The Prime Minister said that the priority for the Slovak government will be to replenish the arsenals of the Slovak Armed Forces and strengthen air defense.

At the end of October, the new Prime Minister of Slovakia, Fico, confirmed that "he will speak in Brussels against any sanctions against Russia until the financial consequences of the imposition of these sanctions are calculated," and spoke out against the supply of weapons to Ukraine. Earlier, he also promised to use the right of veto in the event of Ukraine's possible accession to NATO and spoke out against Ukraine's accession to the EU.

11. Slovak Foreign Minister does not believe in ending war in Ukraine on battlefield

There is no military solution to Russia's war against Ukraine, and therefore it is necessary to work on a political and diplomatic settlement.

Juraj Blanár, the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Slovakia, said this at a press conference in Prague on Monday after meeting with his Czech counterpart Jan Lipavský, Ukrinform reported citing APA. "Prolonging the conflict will not lead to its resolution. The senseless killings must stop," he said.

According to the minister, political discussions and peace initiatives are needed now, "regardless of where they come from."

In this context, Blanár confirmed Slovakia's already declared intention to no longer send weapons to Ukraine. According to him, there is nothing left in the country that can be transferred, and the country must take care of its own security.

At the same time, the minister said that Slovakia condemns Russian aggression against Ukraine as a violation of international law.

12. Ukraine should remain priority in Lithuania's foreign policy - Nauseda

Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda has that while the international community's attention is drawn to new global conflicts, Lithuania's diplomatic efforts should be aimed at mobilizing international support for Ukraine.

He said this after a meeting with Lithuanian diplomats, Ukrinform reports, citing LRT. "Ukraine has had and will have existential significance for us. And all the efforts of the diplomatic agency should be focused on this priority," Nauseda said.

13. EU leaders to propose starting membership talks with Ukraine, Moldova - Reuters

The European Union executive will recommend on Wednesday that the bloc opens membership negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova once they meet outstanding conditions. This was reported by Reuters with reference to own sources, according to Ukrinform. It is noted that the expected EU recommendations will mean that formal negotiations with Kyiv and Chisinau could start next year.
More https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/3783594-eu-leaders-to-propose-starting-membership-talks-with-ukraine-moldova-reuters.html

14. Ukraine expects positive EU appraisal of membership bid - Stefanishyna

Ukraine expects a positive European Union appraisal of its progress on the path towards EU membership in a report due this week.

Ukraine's Deputy Prime Minister for European and Euro-Atlantic Integration Olha Stefanishyna said this in an interview with Reuters, Ukrinform reports. "I would say that the assessment would definitely be positive because we have been in permanent contact with the European Commission, discussing the steps and negotiating the steps we managed to implement," Stefanishyna said.
More https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/3783516-ukraine-expects-positive-eu-appraisal-of-membership-bid-stefanishyna.html

15. Metsola on support for Ukraine: We cannot afford fatigue, it is about security of Europe

The European Union countries cannot allow fatigue from providing support for Ukraine, where the future of European security is now being decided.

President of the European Parliament Roberta Metsola said this in her address to the EU Ambassadors in Brussels on Monday, according to an Ukrinform correspondent.

Ukraine continues to suffer from Russia s illegal invasion into its territory. We know what is at stake there (in this war ed.). Millions of Europeans know from experience exactly what Ukraine is fighting for. And so, when we say, and I am sure you are asked this often, that our support for Ukraine will not waiver, we mean it. We cannot allow fatigue to set in. It is about the security of Europe as well as the security of Ukraine, Metsola said.

16. Anti-Ukraine party gathers strength in Romania

Voter support for illiberal AUR is growing ahead of elections next year
More https://www.ft.com/content/31af3e55-97f7-4bc2-a4e6-89ed2c0c461e

17. Full restoration of Mariupol will take 20 years - mayor

It will take 20 years to fully restore Mariupol city, according to Mariupol Mayor Vadym Boychenko.

The Mariupol City Council posted this on Telegram, Ukrinform reports. "As to the Mariupol Reborn plan, it consists of two parts. The Rapid Action Plan envisages 2 years and 154 projects. As to the full revival of the city to the pre-war population, it will take 20 years. We have appealed to our European partners to help us determine clear deadlines and costs," Boychenko said.
More https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-economy/3783268-full-restoration-of-mariupol-will-take-20-years-mayor.html

18. Life on the frontline in Kherson: dodging shells, facing death and refusing to leave

Amid ceaseless bombardment, Kherson residents shop at the market, clean their homes, and document the horrors of wa
More https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/nov/07/kherson-residents-frontline-bombardment

19. Trump declines Zelenskyy's invitation to visit Ukraine

Former US President Donald Trump declined a visit to Ukraine in response to the invitation of his Ukrainian colleague Volodymyr Zelenskyy. I have great respect for President Zelenskyy, but I think it would be inappropriate to go to Ukraine at this time, Trump said on NBC in response to Zelenskyy's invitation.

According to him, the Biden administration is now dealing with Zelenskyy, and he would not want to create a conflict of interest. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reportedly said he would need 24 minutes to explain to Donald Trump that he cannot control this war.

20. Ukraine war: stalemate on the battlefield and shaky international support putting pressure on Zelensky

More than 20 months into the war in Ukraine and over five months into Ukraine s latest counteroffensive, the situation on the front is bleak and no breakthrough imminent, the country s commander-in-chief admitted in a recent interview with the Economist.
More https://theconversation.com/ukraine-war-stalemate-on-the-battlefield-and-shaky-international-support-putting-pressure-on-zelensky-216930

21. Zelensky s Worst Week? Here s What Happened

From scandalous allegations in Western publications to his general s comments about the war hitting a stalemate, President Zelensky may have had the most tumultuous week of his presidency.
More https://www.kyivpost.com/post/23754

22. Zaluzhny's assistant killed by grenade explosion near Kyiv police

A serviceman has been killed in a residential complex in the village of Chaiky, Kyiv region, as a result of careless handling of ammunition, the press service of the National Police of Ukraine reports. "According to preliminary information, a 39-year-old serviceman was killed as a result of a grenade explosion. His 13-year-old son is seriously injured. The guy is under the supervision of doctors," the message posted on Facebook says.

The police are working at the scene. Criminal proceedings have been initiated on the fact of the death of a person and illegal handling of ammunition.

As law enforcement sources told Interfax-Ukraine, the deceased serviceman worked as an assistant to Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Valeriy Zaluzhny. It is also noted that during the search of the apartment, the police found another five grenades.

23. Death of Zaluzhnyi's aide most likely an accident - source

The death of Hennadii Chastiakov, an aide to Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Valerii Zaluzhnyi, was most likely the result of an accident.

A source in the law enforcement agencies told this to Ukrinform. "This is a tragic accident with a probability of 99.9%. He was presented with combat grenades for his birthday, and one of them detonated due to careless handling," the source said.

24. Police find officer who gifted live grenades to Zaluzhnyi s aide

Ukrainian police have identified the colleague of Hennadiy Chastyakov who gave him a birthday present of several live grenades, Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko announced on Nov. 6.

Chastyakov died in his home near Kyiv when one of the grenades exploded earlier on Nov. 6. He served as an aide to Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Valerii Zaluzhnyi.
More https://english.nv.ua/nation/police-find-officer-who-gifted-live-grenades-to-zaluzhnyi-s-aide-50366237.html

25. EXPLAINED: How a Birthday Gift Grenade Killed General Zaluzhny s Assistant

Early reports suggested it was possible assassination but Ukrainian law enforcement sources quickly dismissed the idea and instead described it as a tragic accident.
More https://www.kyivpost.com/post/23759
